paths.title: CI/CD, Deployment & Release Engineering
paths.description: Turn fast AI-generated changes into controlled, repeatable releases with gated validation, immutable artifacts, migrations, and rollback.

lessons.title: Run CI on every proposed change
lessons.principle: Automated validation should precede integration.
lessons.practice: Trigger lint, types, tests, builds, and policy checks for pull requests.

lessons.title: Make required checks authoritative
lessons.principle: Optional green badges do not protect the default branch.
lessons.practice: Configure branch rules so critical checks must pass on the current head.

lessons.title: Build once and promote
lessons.principle: Rebuilding per environment can produce different artifacts.
lessons.practice: Create a versioned immutable artifact in CI and promote the same artifact through environments.

lessons.title: Use environment-specific configuration
lessons.principle: Artifacts should remain stable while runtime settings change.
lessons.practice: Inject configuration and secrets per environment rather than rebuilding source.

lessons.title: Protect deployment credentials
lessons.principle: CI tokens often have broad infrastructure access.
lessons.practice: Use short-lived identity, least privilege, protected environments, and secret masking.

lessons.title: Separate preview, staging, and production
lessons.principle: Different environments answer different questions.
lessons.practice: Use previews for change inspection, staging for integration, and production for real traffic.

lessons.title: Automate database migration order
lessons.principle: Schema and application versions must overlap safely.
lessons.practice: Run expand migrations before dependent code and defer destructive contraction until old versions are gone.

lessons.title: Use deployment health checks
lessons.principle: A successful upload does not mean the application works.
lessons.practice: Verify readiness, key endpoints, dependencies, and representative user flows after deployment.

lessons.title: Use progressive rollout for risk
lessons.principle: Exposing everyone at once increases blast radius.
lessons.practice: Use canary, percentage, ring, or feature-flag rollout for consequential changes.

lessons.title: Define rollback triggers
lessons.principle: Operators need objective conditions for stopping a rollout.
lessons.practice: Tie rollback to error rate, latency, health, or critical business failures.

lessons.title: Know when rollback is unsafe
lessons.principle: Database and external side effects may not reverse with application code.
lessons.practice: Design forward fixes or compatible migrations for irreversible changes.

lessons.title: Version releases
lessons.principle: Operational state should map to source and artifacts.
lessons.practice: Record commit SHA, build identifier, dependency set, and release metadata.

lessons.title: Generate release notes from intent
lessons.principle: Commit lists alone may not explain user impact.
lessons.practice: Summarize features, fixes, migrations, known issues, and operator actions.

lessons.title: Protect production environments
lessons.principle: Deployment should require appropriate authorization.
lessons.practice: Use environment approvals or protected branches for sensitive releases.

lessons.title: Avoid manual snowflake deploys
lessons.principle: Unrecorded dashboard changes create drift.
lessons.practice: Put deployment steps, infrastructure, and configuration in version-controlled automation where practical.

lessons.title: Capture deployment telemetry
lessons.principle: Release events should be visible in observability tools.
lessons.practice: Annotate metrics and logs with version and deploy time to correlate regressions.

lessons.title: Test rollback procedures
lessons.principle: A theoretical rollback can fail under pressure.
lessons.practice: Exercise artifact rollback, configuration restoration, and data recovery in non-production.

lessons.title: Clean up preview resources
lessons.principle: Ephemeral environments can leak cost and data.
lessons.practice: Expire branches, databases, buckets, and temporary credentials automatically.

lessons.title: Post-deploy smoke test
lessons.principle: CI cannot detect every environment-specific problem.
lessons.practice: Run focused production-safe checks after rollout and verify critical flows.

lessons.title: Close the release loop
lessons.principle: Shipping is complete only when the new version is healthy.
lessons.practice: Confirm telemetry, migrations, errors, and user-impact metrics before declaring release success.

codeExamples.snippet:
name: validate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

paths.title: Observability, Reliability & Operations
paths.description: Design AI-generated services so operators can detect, explain, and recover from failures after deployment.

lessons.title: Define service objectives
lessons.principle: Reliability should reflect user-visible expectations.
lessons.practice: Choose indicators and targets for availability, latency, correctness, or freshness.

lessons.title: Use structured logs
lessons.principle: Free-form text is difficult to query consistently.
lessons.practice: Emit machine-readable events with level, operation, correlation, outcome, and safe context.

lessons.title: Preserve correlation IDs
lessons.principle: One user action may cross many services.
lessons.practice: Propagate request or trace identifiers through logs, queues, and external calls.

lessons.title: Measure golden signals
lessons.principle: Basic service health needs a small set of high-value metrics.
lessons.practice: Track traffic, errors, latency, and saturation for important services.

lessons.title: Use traces for distributed work
lessons.principle: Cross-service latency is hard to reconstruct from isolated logs.
lessons.practice: Instrument meaningful spans and propagate trace context.

lessons.title: Log business-critical events
lessons.principle: Infrastructure health can be green while product behavior fails.
lessons.practice: Measure outcomes such as successful checkout, upload, sync, or job completion.

lessons.title: Avoid logging secrets
lessons.principle: Observability data often has broad access and retention.
lessons.practice: Redact credentials, tokens, sensitive payloads, and unnecessary personal data.

lessons.title: Create actionable alerts
lessons.principle: Alerts should represent conditions that need human or automated action.
lessons.practice: Tie alerts to service objectives, sustained failures, or resource exhaustion rather than noisy single events.

lessons.title: Include runbook links
lessons.principle: An alert without response guidance wastes incident time.
lessons.practice: Link likely causes, dashboards, safe diagnostics, mitigation, and escalation.

lessons.title: Separate liveness and readiness
lessons.principle: Restart and traffic-routing decisions answer different questions.
lessons.practice: Use liveness for stuck processes and readiness for whether a process should receive work.

lessons.title: Use health checks sparingly
lessons.principle: Health endpoints can create cascading dependency checks.
lessons.practice: Check only dependencies needed to safely accept the relevant work.

lessons.title: Track deployment versions
lessons.principle: Incidents often correlate with releases.
lessons.practice: Include version or commit metadata in logs, metrics, and traces.

lessons.title: Monitor queues and background jobs
lessons.principle: Async systems can fail silently while APIs remain healthy.
lessons.practice: Track age, depth, throughput, retries, dead letters, and failure reasons.

lessons.title: Monitor database saturation
lessons.principle: Database limits often become system-wide bottlenecks.
lessons.practice: Watch connections, locks, slow queries, replication, storage, and transaction latency.

lessons.title: Plan incident roles
lessons.principle: Major failures need coordinated decision making.
lessons.practice: Define incident lead, communication, operations, and subject-matter roles before an outage.

lessons.title: Use blameless postmortems
lessons.principle: The goal is to improve systems, not hide mistakes.
lessons.practice: Document timeline, contributing conditions, detection gaps, response, and preventive actions.

lessons.title: Test disaster recovery
lessons.principle: Backups and replicas do not guarantee recoverability.
lessons.practice: Exercise restore, failover, credentials, DNS, and dependency reconstruction.

lessons.title: Track error budgets
lessons.principle: Reliability targets should influence delivery decisions.
lessons.practice: Use consumed error budget to decide when to prioritize resilience over feature velocity.

lessons.title: Remove noisy telemetry
lessons.principle: Too much low-value data raises cost and obscures important signals.
lessons.practice: Regularly review dashboards, logs, and alerts for usefulness.

lessons.title: Operate what you generate
lessons.principle: AI-assisted development still creates ongoing operational ownership.
lessons.practice: Ensure the team can diagnose, mitigate, and recover the systems it chooses to deploy.

codeExamples.snippet:
alerts:
  - name: high-error-rate
    condition: error_rate > 0.02 for 10m
    runbook: /runbooks/high-error-rate.md
